Q: lifetime of an array created element by element A:

The operator new[] used to allocate the storage to which Storage points does implicitly create objects, but since the new operator then creates an array of store_t there, no such object can survive until the pointer arithmetic on reinterpret_cast<data_t*>(ptr). Without an array object, that arithmetic is undefined. You could try to use pointer arithmetic on the bytes underlying the array, but the standard remains unclear on that point (though remedies are in progress) and the resulting objects would not be members of an array (absent explicitly creating one) even if they had adjacent addresses.

Q: gdb - get variable name of register A:

I can see why you'd want to do this, for example if you're not sure from the disassembly and register states alone which variable corresponds to which register at any given time. at any given time is the keyword here.

As said earlier, the correspondence between variables and registers isn't 1:1 at all. However, at every step the debugger, assuming gdb here, should be aware where the variable lives if it isn't optimized away. And to query that state, you run:

(gdb) info address my_reg
Symbol "my_reg" is a variable in $rdi.

The second line is example output.

For more details, check (gdb) help info. Hope that helps!

Q: How can I find the earliest unrepeated character in Python more efficiently? A:

Here's an alternative, though I'm not sure if it's the fastest one. (In my tests, it seems to take half the time of Booboo's implementation, but since I'm not very “good” at Python, I'll allow myself to have my doubts.)

def first_unique_char( word ):
    statics = [ 0 ] * 26
    
    for letter in word:
        statics[ ord( letter ) - 97 ] += 1

    for letter in word:
        if statics[ ord( letter ) - 97 ] == 1:
            return letter
            
    return None
    
words = [
    'leetcodee',
    'loveleetcode',
    'aabb'
]

  # code used for comparisons:
t1 = time.time()
for _ in range( 10000 ):
    for word in words:
        first_unique_char( word )
print( time.time() - t1 )

Note: As Kelly Bundy rightly points out, when using something like this as a string:

s = ‘a’ * 10**5

my approach takes about twice as long. I can't quite figure out why there's this difference, but there it is.

Q: Why does Keycloak use a Session-Cookie instead of JWT Authorization Header A:

You write:

When I want to access a protected resource I am shown the Keycloak login form and can log in. I get redirected to the resource after login.

This leads me to assume you're using a browser and issuing a GET request. I'm assuming the browser is using the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant Type, and so the tokens are exchanged between the client (the web server) and the Keycloak server. And not between the web browser and the web server. This is a decision that was made by the team developing the "protected resource" and not something you can change without changing the source code of the "protected resource".

You also write:

In the request header I can see that the header Cookie: mongo-express=s%3AVpTxrBrZp_bb1kpZOuCo6nitgpTzI0YJ.6OS1ttu4hjcnut%2FG6zdyDnLk2B%2FrEmMEEw9jy2rCUrE; SESSION=510eb294-493e-4cb6-9cb8-1e09604a7fc7 is set.

If you start a browser form scratch (or use e.g. "New Incognito Window" in Chrome or "New Private Window" in Firefox) I'm pretty sure you'll see that in the response to the very first GET request to the protected resource, you'll find a Set-Cookie HTTP header in the server response (presumably the one that redirects to the OAuth2 server). This is just how the protected resource manages its sessions. Not much you can do about that, I'm affraid.

Q: Azure Active Directory Authorization "The access token is from the wrong issuer ' A:

The reason for this is : we authenticated against the common tenant, but now we're trying access data from a subscription which belongs to a separate tenant - and we don't have an AccessToken for this new tenant.

What we have to do in this case is acquire a new AccessToken (a JWT) for the same user and client ID, but authorising against the tenant for the subscription we selected.

i.e. we have an AccessToken , but it's a common tenant AccessToken , and therefore is limited in what is authorised: to work with resources that are specific to a particular subscription, we now need an AccessToken for that specific subscription and tenant.

To do this, we just need to use the TenantId of the subscription the User selected instead of using a Tenant of "common".

See the step 3 at http://www.bizbert.com/bizbert/2015/11/16/Listing+Subscriptions+And+Logic+Apps+From+NET.aspx for details.

Q: Installing Facebook APK in Genymotion A:

Follow these steps.

  1. Change PATH system variable to path of tool i.e. parent-Directories/to/tools.
    Go to My Computer-->Properties-->Advances System Settings-->System Variables-->PATH.

  2. RUN-->cmd and change your current directory to /tool ( tools directory should have adb.exe ) http://www.wikihow.com/Change-Directories-in-Command-Prompt

  3. Install just one virtual device in Genymotion Virtual Device Manager and run that virtual device.

  4. Run the command, adb install full-path/yourAPK.apk

  5. In case of more installed virtual devices, your fourth step would be
    adb -e install full-path/yourAPK.apk
